Rashi on Ketubot 27a:10:1.english: Sentries - The place where the guards stand, whom the king stationed so that no one would harm the people of the city.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:10:2.hebrew: דמהדר למתא כו' - שמו סביבות העיר שלשלות ברזל, שישמיעו קול בהכשל איש רץ עליהם, וכלבים ואווזים זועקין:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:10:2.english: Where they surround the city, etc. - They placed iron chains around the city, so that they would make a sound when a running man stumbles over them, and dogs and geese cry out.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:10:3.english: And branches [gavza] - sticks and twigs to stumble over.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:11:1.hebrew: ולא קשיא ליה מידי - לא חייש למיעקר איניש יחידאה ולבעול, הואיל ואין הדבר הפקר:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:11:1.english: And it is not difficult for him at all - He is not concerned about a single person detaching himself and engaging in intercourse, since the matter is not a free-for-all.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:14:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא משני שבילין - דכיון דבא לשאול עליו ועל חבירו, אמר רבי יוסי טמאין; הכא נמי, לכולהו שרינן כי הדדי:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:14:1.english: And in what [way] is [this] different from two paths - For since he came to ask about himself and about his fellow, Rabbi Yosei said [they are] impure; here too, [do] we permit all of them together?

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:14:2.hebrew: אחד טמא - שיש בו קברות מפסיק כל רחבו, ואין ידוע איזהו הטמא, אבל כך מוחזקים באחד מהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:14:2.english: One [that was] ritually impure - [Meaning] that it has graves spanning its entire width, and it is not known which one is the impure [path], but it is thus established regarding one of them.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:14:3.english: And prepared ritually pure items - [He] touched ritually pure items.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:15:1.hebrew: טהורים - דכל חד כי אתי לקמן, תלינן ליה למימר בטהור הלך, דהוה ליה ספק טומאה בר"ה וספיקו טהור:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:15:1.english: [They are] pure - For each one, when he comes before us, we attribute [it] to him to say [that] he walked on the pure [path], since it is [a case of] uncertain ritual impurity in the public domain, and its uncertainty is pure.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:15:2.hebrew: טמאין - דהיכי נימא להו טהורים אתם? חד מינייהו ודאי בטמא אזל:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:15:2.english: They are impure - For how could we say to them, "You are pure"? One of them certainly walked on the impure [path].

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:16:1.english: At the same time - They came to ask at the same time.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:16:2.hebrew: הכא נמי כו' - ור' יהודה ור' יוסי, הלכה כר' יוסי:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:16:2.english: Here too, etc. - And [between] Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yosei, the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:1:1.hebrew: הורהנה - דמדעת, וכיון דהגיע זמן ולא נפדית, הרי היא של עובדי כוכבים בדיניהם; משום הכי בעינן עדים מעידין אותה שלא נסתרה:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:1:1.english: She was taken as security - For [she was pledged] with consent, and once the time [for payment] arrived and she was not redeemed, she belongs to the idolaters according to their laws; therefore, we require witnesses testifying about her that she did not enter into seclusion.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:1:2.hebrew: נחבשה - דאינה נחלטת להם, לא בעינן עדים, הואיל ועל ידי ממון הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:1:2.english: [If] she was imprisoned - Since she is not forfeited to them, we do not require witnesses, as it is on account of money.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:4:1.hebrew: ואיכא דרמי לה מרמא - לא מתני לה להא דרב שמואל בר רב יצחק אפירושא דמתניתין בלשון לא שנו, אלא רמי מירמא מתניתין וברייתא אהדדי, ועלה שני רב שמואל חילוק בין יד ישראל תקיפה ליד העובדי כוכבים תקיפה:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:4:1.english: And there are those who raise it as a contradiction - [They] do not teach this [statement] of Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak as an explanation of the Mishnah with the phrasing "they only taught [this]"; rather, they raise a contradiction between the Mishnah and the Baraita against each other, and regarding it Rav Shmuel teaches the distinction between [when] the hand of Israel is strong and [when] the hand of the idolaters is strong.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:6:1.hebrew: הני נשי דגנבי - שבעליהן ניתלין, ודרך המלכות להפקיר ביתם ונשיהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:6:1.english: These wives of thieves - For their husbands are hanged, and [it is] the practice of the government to declare their house and their wives ownerless.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:6:2.hebrew: בן דונאי - רוצח היה ואלעזר שמו, כדאמרינן בפ' עגלה ערופה (סוטה מז.). אבל נשי דגנבי הגונבים ממון לא מפקרי:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:6:2.english: Ben Donai - He was a murderer, and his name was Elazar, as we say in the chapter [entitled] Eglah Arufah (Sotah 47a). However, the wives of thieves who steal money are not abandoned [to all].

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:7:1.english: Karkom [siege] - [The Hebrew word] matzor [siege] is translated [in Aramaic as] karkoma (Deuteronomy 20).

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:7:2.hebrew: פסולות - אסורות לבעליהן, דאשת כהן אסורה באונס:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:7:2.english: Unfit - [They are] forbidden to their husbands, for the wife of a priest is forbidden [even] through rape.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:8:1.hebrew: בלשת - חיל, על שם שמחפשים כל המטמונים:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:8:1.english: A military unit [baleshet] - An armed troop, [so called] because they search all the hidden treasures.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:9:1.english: To engage in intercourse there is respite - For their desire overpowers them.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:9:2.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar said - Even regarding intercourse, there are times when they [the women] are permitted.

Rashi on Ketubot 27a:9:3.hebrew: כרכום של אותה מלכות - אינו רוצה להשחית את בני העיר, וכשכובש עיר הסמוך לממשלתו, שומרה והיא לו למס עובד:
Rashi on Ketubot 27a:9:3.english: A siege of the same monarchy - [The king] does not want to destroy the inhabitants of the city, and when he conquers a city adjacent to his dominion, he preserves it, and it becomes tributary to him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:14:1.hebrew: והלך באחד מהם ועשה טהרות - להכי נקט "ועשה טהרות", דלענין האדם אנו מזקיקים שניהם לטבול ולהזות, פן יבואו לידי טומאה ודאי אם יגעו שניהם בככר אחד; לכך אומר להו: "זילו טבילו, דהא נהרא קמייכו". ועוד, דמשום דבעי למתני סיפא: "הזה וטבל — טהור, הלך בשני ועשה טהרות — הרי אלו טהורות; ואם קיימות הראשונים — אלו ואלו תלויות; ואם לא טהר בינתים — הראשונות תלויות והשניות ישרפו":
Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:14:1.english: And [one] walked on one of them and handled ritually pure items - This is why [the Mishnah] stated "and handled ritually pure items": because with respect to the person [himself], we require both of them to immerse and undergo sprinkling [with purification water], lest they come to definite ritual impurity if both of them touch one loaf; therefore one says to them: "Go immerse, for behold, the river is before you." And furthermore, [it stated this] because [the Tanna] wanted to teach the latter clause: "[If] he was sprinkled and immersed, [he is] pure; [if] he [then] walked on the second [path] and handled ritually pure items, these are pure. And if the first [items] are still extant, both these and those are suspended [in doubt]; and if he did not purify himself in between, the first [items] are suspended and the second [items] must be burned."

Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:15:1.hebrew: ואם נשאל זה בפני עצמו וזה בפני עצמו טהורות - לא שיאכלם אדם אחד, דאם כן יאכל ודאי טומאה, דהכי אמרינן בשבועות בפ"ב (דף יט.): הלך בראשון ולא נכנס, בשני ונכנס — חייב, דטמא הוא ממה נפשך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:15:1.english: "And if this [one] asked in and of himself and that [one] asked in and of himself, they are pure" - [This does] not [mean] that one person may eat them [both], for if so, he would certainly be eating [something with] ritual impurity, for so we say in Shevuot in the second chapter (19a): "[If] he walked on the first [path] and did not enter [the Temple], [and then walked] on the second [path] and entered, he is liable, for he is ritually impure either way."

Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:16:1.hebrew: בבא לישאל עליו ועל חברו - אין לפרש שבא לישאל בבת אחת, דהתם מודו כולי עלמא דטמאות, מכל שכן דבאו לישאל שניהם בבת אחת; אלא מיירי ששאל על עצמו וטהרוהו, ואח"כ בא לישאל על חבירו, דמר מדמי ליה לבת אחת כיון ששאל על שניהם במעמד אחד, ומר מדמי ליה לזה אחר זה כיון שטיהרוהו קודם. והכא נמי כיון דשרו לכולהו — כבת אחת דמי; אף על פי שאין בא לפנינו אלא על אחת, מ"מ הדבר ידוע לכל שהרבה כהנות היו, והוי כאילו בא לישאל על כולם בבת אחת, והכא מודו כ"ע, ובחנם דחק בקונטרס לפרש כר' יוסי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:16:1.english: [With regard to one who] comes to ask about himself and about his fellow - One should not explain [this as meaning] that he came to ask [about both] at the same time, for in that case everyone agrees that they are impure — all the more so when both of them came to ask at the same time. Rather, it refers to a case where he asked about himself and they declared him pure, and afterward he came to ask about his fellow; for one Sage likens it to [asking] at the same time, since he asked about both of them in a single session, while the other Sage likens it to one after the other, since they had already declared him pure beforehand. And here too, since they permit all of them — it is tantamount to [asking] at the same time; even though [someone] only comes before us regarding one [woman], nevertheless it is known to all that there were many wives of priests, so it is as if he came to ask about all of them at the same time, and here everyone agrees, and in vain did the Kuntres [Rashi] force [himself] to explain [the Gemara] according to Rabbi Yosei.

Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:9:1.hebrew: כאן בכרכום של אותה מלכות - פי' שיושבין בטח לפי שאין אחריהן מחנה, ויש פנאי לנסך ולבעול; אבל בלשת של מלכות אחרת, שאימת מלכות שבאו בגבולה עליהם, אין להן פנאי. וכן פי' ר"ח ור"ת, וכן מוכח בירושלמי. ופריך: כרכום של אותה מלכות — אי אפשר דלא ערקא חדא מינייהו! והוה לן למשרינהו לכולהו ולמיתלי לקולא, דבשבויה הקילו, כדאמרינן בסמוך: "אם יש מחבואה אחת מצלת על כל הכהנות כולן"; אע"ג דמספקא לן באינה מחזקת אלא אחת — הכא פשיטא לן דשרו, דהתם לא ודאי נחבאת, אבל הכא ודאי ערקא. ולפי' הקונטרס קשה טובא: חדא, דפריך נתלי לחומרא, וגבי מחבואה תלינן לקולא; ועוד, דמה מתרץ "דמהדר למתא כו'" ואין אדם נכנס לשם — והא קתני "בלשת שנכנסה לעיר"! ועוד, כיון דאההיא דע"ז פריך, הוה ליה למימר "אי אפשר דלא ערק חד מינייהו ונסך"! ועוד, דהתם מפרש טעמא "לפי שאין פנאי לנסך", ולית ליה טעמא לפי שאין כרכום של אותה מלכות רוצה להשחית את בני העיר. [ועוד, מאי שנא שעת מלחמה משעת שלום?] ויש ליישב לפי שיטת הקונטרס: דרבי יצחק בן אלעזר לא אתי לשנויי מתני' אההיא דע"ז, אלא אית ליה שינוייא דרב מרי, ומתניתין דהתם נמי בכרכום של מלכות אחרת, ולא בא אלא לפרושי מתניתין. וכן משמע בפרק בתרא דע"ז (דף עא.), דפריך התם ממתניתין דהכא אמתניתין דבלשת, ולא מייתי התם דרבי יצחק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 27a:9:1.english: Here, in a siege of the same monarchy - [This] means that they sit securely because there is no [enemy] army behind them, and [thus] they have respite to pour [wine for idolatry] and to engage in intercourse; whereas [in the case of] a military unit of a different monarchy, where the fear of the monarchy whose border they have entered is upon them, they have no respite [for either]. And so explained Rabbeinu Ḥananel and Rabbeinu Tam, and so it is proven in the Jerusalem Talmud. And [the Gemara] asks: "In a siege of the same monarchy, it is impossible that one of them [i.e., one of the women] did not flee!" And we should permit all of them and attribute [their survival] leniently, for regarding a captive woman [the Sages] were lenient, as we say nearby: "If there is one hideaway, it saves all the women [married to] priests." Even though there we are in doubt when it holds only one [woman], here it is obvious to us that they are permitted, for there it is not certain that [any woman] hid, whereas here it is certain that [at least one] fled. And according to the explanation of the Kuntres [Rashi], it is very difficult: First, that [the Gemara] asks that we should attribute stringently, whereas regarding a hideaway we attribute leniently; and furthermore, what does it answer, "where they surround the city, etc." [such that] no person enters there — why, [the mishna in Avodah Zarah] teaches "a military unit that entered a city"! And furthermore, since [according to Rashi] it is asking on that [mishna] of Avodah Zarah, it should have said: "It is impossible that one of them did not slip away and pour [wine for idolatry]"! And furthermore, there [in Avodah Zarah] it explains the reason [as being] "because there is no respite to pour," and it does not have the reason "because a siege of the same monarchy does not want to destroy the inhabitants of the city." [And furthermore, what is the difference between wartime and peacetime?] However, one can resolve [it] according to the approach of the Kuntres [Rashi]: that Rabbi Yitzḥak ben Elazar did not come to reconcile our mishna with that [mishna] of Avodah Zarah; rather, he holds the resolution of Rav Mari, and the mishna there [in Avodah Zarah] also [deals] with a siege of a different monarchy, and he only came to explain our mishna. And so it is implied in the last chapter of Avodah Zarah (71a), where [the Gemara] asks there from our mishna here against the mishna of the military unit, and it does not cite there [the statement] of Rabbi Yitzḥak:
